column2: A master of Cremona who learned his craft close to the Stradivari workshop.
A master who moved from city to city. Much prized for his powerful sound.
By the founder of the Brescian school. Ole Bull played a carved example.
J.B. Vuillaume (copy of a great instrument)
The great maker and dealer of Paris. His copies of Stradivari were so fine as to be all but indistinguishable from the originals.
Napoleon is said to have tried it and scratched it with the spur of his boot.
The maker called 'the Lion of Venice'. A broad, rich sound.
A light bow curving outwards. Suited to short, singing notes.
The transitional bow favoured by Cramer in London, a bridge to the modern bow.
By the bow maker called 'the English Tourte'.
'The Stradivari of the bow', who perfected the modern form. Pernambuco wood and an inward curve gave a long, powerful tone.
A great bow maker who learned his craft in Vuillaume's workshop.
The great bow maker of St Petersburg, called 'the Russian Tourte'.
A slender, supple bow for a new age.
A powerful bow, loved by the great violinists of the 20th century.
A common bow, to be had at any workshop.
The great London firm. In 1818 one was presented to Beethoven.
The Viennese master, known for the piano of Beethoven's last years and the one Schumann gave to Clara.
The great Viennese firm, founded in 1828. It made its name by surviving Liszt's ferocious playing.
The great Berlin firm, founded in 1853. Played by Bülow and Liszt.
Every Cremonese instrument leaves my shop with my certificate.
With a Hill certificate, it will be accepted wherever you go.

I devised a trumpet with keys myself.
A trumpet that can play semitones, for your orchestra.
Trumpeter of the Viennese court. He developed the keyed trumpet, and Haydn wrote his concerto for the instrument.
The horn with pistons is the instrument of the future.
The new horn, for your orchestra.
A pioneer of the valve (piston) horn. He taught the valve horn at the Paris Conservatoire from 1833.
The horn solo in Beethoven's Ninth
I am a horn player of the Kärntnertortheater.
The horn of Vienna, for your orchestra.
A celebrated Viennese horn player, said to have played the famous horn solo of the third movement at the premiere of Beethoven's Ninth.
Maestro Wagner has taken a liking to my large viola.
The sound of the viola alta, for your orchestra.
The player who devised the large 'viola alta'. Invited by Wagner, he played at the first Bayreuth Festival in 1876.
Cornet solo: The Carnival of Venice
The king of the cornet, for your orchestra.
Star cornettist of Sousa's band. His studies of transcendent difficulty are still the brass player's bible.
The horn parts of Brahms's symphonies
Thirty years of horn at the Gewandhaus.
The horn of Leipzig, for your orchestra.
Principal horn of the Gewandhaus Orchestra and a great teacher, known for his orchestral studies for horn.
the trumpet virtuoso of Bach's own town
For great violas, look to the Brescian school: a deep, large sound.
Only about ten Stradivari violas survive.
A masterpiece of the Raoux workshop in Paris. Punto is said to have played a Raoux horn of silver.
The old horn, whose pitch is altered with the hand in the bell.
The horn with valves, born about 1818. Semitones come easily.
Developed by Weidinger: a trumpet that produces semitones by means of keys.
A brass instrument with pistons, born in Paris about 1828. A star instrument of the 19th century.
A long trumpet without valves. Playing melodies in its high register took a virtuoso.
I came from Japan to study music! Please let me in!

A student from Japan who somehow turns up in every era of Europe. He does not count the beat, but the destructive power of his funny faces is the greatest on the continent. He changes the mood of the house in an instant.
'My party piece' (the title changes every time)
When I was young, mind you, 'concertmaster' meant me.
This orchestra would never hold together without me, eh?

An elderly fiddler who has taken up residence in the orchestra. Generous with intonation, but in theory and old stories he yields to no one. He has no intention of giving up the concertmaster's chair.
On the night you get one shot. If it cracks, that is music too.
With my horn I shall lend this orchestra some gravitas.
A horn player of long standing. The cracked first note is a tradition by now, and the audience waits for it with bated breath. Plenty of old stories, too.
Flute concerto (the music is at home)
Oh — the music… I am sure I brought it.
I forget things, but my playing is sound! Probably.
A flautist who forgets the music, the stand, and sometimes the instrument itself. Not good at counting rests, either.
